The test image shows soybean plants with severe lower stem damage — dark/blackened tissue at the base, dead/dried plant material, with some collapse near the soil line. Key features to investigate: dark stem lesions at the lower nodes/base, late-season appearance.

Top candidates: Anthracnose, Phytophthora, Charcoal_Rot, Diaporthe. Let me view reference images.

Now I have enough reference data. Let me analyze the test image systematically:

**Test image observations:**
- Late-season soybean plants with significant lower stem damage
- Very dark, nearly black discoloration at the lower stem/base area
- Orange-brown coloration visible in the center of the dark stem (decaying pith)
- Dead/dried plant material with leaves still attached
- Some green stems in the foreground (partial/neighboring plants still alive)
- Overall plant collapse pattern from the base

**Key comparisons:**
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Upper-right panel in reference shows nearly black stem cross-section (microsclerotia-laden tissue), dead plants with leaves remaining attached — strongly matches
- **Anthracnose**: Late-season dark blotches on stems — possible but test image lacks the characteristic reddish-brown coloration and shows more diffuse dark tissue
- **Phytophthora**: Dark brown lesion from taproot — plausible, but test shows more extensive dark discoloration
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Dark taproot with blue fungal growth — SDS reference lower-left is close, but SDS typically has interveinal leaf chlorosis which isn't evident here
- **Diaporthe/Fusarium/Rhizoctonia**: Don't match the extent and pattern of dark stem decay seen here

**Conclusion:** The very dark/charcoal-like lower stem discoloration, late-season plant death with leaves still attached, and overall pattern of stem/root decay at the soil line most closely matches **Charcoal_Rot**. The black microsclerotia give the stem that near-black charcoal texture visible in the test image, consistent with both the description and reference images.
